idiom_name: @Column(() => Name) merging the value class's columns into the owner's table
implementation_notes: TypeORM documents this exact pattern as embedded columns: a class with its own @Column properties is passed to @Column(() => Name) on the owner and all of its columns are merged into the owner's database table, with the column names prefixed by the property name (nameFirst, nameLast). The stated motivation is reducing duplication through composition instead of inheritance, which is Embedded Value's purpose in an ORM; nested embedded classes are supported, and the value class has no primary key of its own.
pitfalls: TypeORM merges the columns without giving the value class an identity, but the embedded object is still a class instance - sharing one instance between two owners writes the same values twice and mutating it changes both.
Relations inside an embedded class are not consistently prefixed (a long-standing issue in TypeORM), so an embedded value that contains a @ManyToOne can collide with the owner's columns.
Two embeddings of the same class in one entity produce duplicate column names; TypeORM does not detect the collision at compile time.

variants.name: MikroORM embeddables (@Embedded with automatic prefixing)
variants.idiom_name: @Embeddable class + @Embedded property with a configurable prefix
variants.implementation_notes: MikroORM inlines all columns of an @Embeddable class into the table of the owning entity 'just as if you had declared them directly there', and prefixes the generated column names with the embedded property name by default (address_street, address_postal_code). Embeddables are queryable, may contain nested @Embedded properties, and from v5 may also hold a @ManyToOne, so the value type is not restricted to primitives. The prefix is configurable per property, which is how the same embeddable is used twice in one entity.
pitfalls: Embeddables must be discovered like entities (registered in the entity list); an unregistered embeddable fails at runtime rather than at startup.
If every field of the embeddable is nullable the property comes back as null instead of an initialized value unless you provide a default (onCreate/initializer).
Prefixes are applied by convention, so renaming the embedded property renames its columns - a migration is required and existing data must be moved with it.
